messages.author: 403a8738ba91e2e5
messages.subject: HMM model for capture-recapture data
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm trying to implement a HMM (aka multievent) model in TMB to analyse capture-recapture data. I'm curious about the performance of TMB compared to Rcpp with which I have already implemented the same model (https://github.com/oliviergimenez/multieventRcpp).

With TMB, I run into compilation errors that I do not seem able to sort out :-( I suspect these errors are related to the way I use indexing by a data vector, and also how I handle element-wise vector multiplications.

The code and data are available from https://github.com/oliviergimenez/hmm_tmb. Any help would be much appreciated.

Cheers,
Olivier

messages.author: 55d0e2f87b0f795e
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] HMM model for capture-recapture data
parts:
Hi Olivier,

I’m happy to see that you’re interested in this and I’m curious about the benchmarking results. I’d really like to see a few models with discrete latent state variables translated into TMB. I was recently working on converting the lady slipper example from Ch 9 of "Bayesian Population Analysis using WinBUGS --- A Hierarchical Perspective" (2012) by Marc Kéry and Michael Schaub. A goal of this exercise would be to compare some the MCMC methods for TMB to those of STAN and WinBUGS.

I’m almost done with the ladyslipper example, and welcome other people to try others from this chapter. Conveniently, the algorithm for calculating the likelihood while integrating over the discrete latent variables is in these stan examples
https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/tree/master/BPA

I hope my pull request on GitHub solves the compilation errors. It might be computationally more efficient to replace this 
- ALPHA = (ALPHA * A) * B.row(evennt(j)); // vector matrix product, then element-wise vector product

with some linear algebra and typecasting, but I was lazy and didn’t think about it very hard. I didn’t try making ALPHA a matrix, but that could be a solution.

cheers,
Mollie

 
———————————
Mollie E. Brooks, Ph.D.
Postdoctoral Researcher
National Institute of Aquatic Resources
Technical University of Denmark
